title: Genotype-phenotype map for the flying-fish blueprint, from proxy fish, at every layer
constraint: Almost no molecular data exists for flying fish (Exocoetidae). NCBI holds one scaffold-level assembly (GCA_018398805.1, Hirundichthys speculiger) and OrthoDB holds no genome for the whole suborder Belonoidei. Every gene link here was measured in a PROXY species, zebrafish (Danio rerio) or medaka (Oryzias latipes, same order Beloniformes as flying fish). None of it is flying-fish data.
causation_warning: Most links are 'expressed in': the gene's RNA or protein was detected in the structure. That is not causation. 'required for' means a single-gene loss-of-function zebrafish has an abnormal phenotype there (or, for GO-based links, that GO places the gene in the structure's developmental process on mutant evidence). 'sufficient for' here means a verified gain-of-function allele changes the structure (e.g. enlarges it); it does not mean the gene makes the structure. No gene 'makes' a fin.

propagation_rules.expressed in: propagates UP part_of: expression in a part implies some expression in what contains it. Marked derived with the path.
propagation_rules.required for: never propagates DOWN. Propagation UP is an inference, marked derived, never presented as observed.
propagation_rules.graph: the blueprint's own part_of placements (organism-design/examples/a-flying-fish.json), which the lean thread kernel-certified as acyclic and rooted, so propagation is well defined and terminates. Bgee's own propagation is excluded: only Bgee calls that include data observed in that very structure are used.

blueprint.pectoral_fin_note: In the blueprint the pectoral fin has one tissue beneath it (mesenchyme pectoral fin) and no cell types. ZFA has 52 terms that are parts of the zebrafish pectoral fin; the blueprint has a node for none of them except the mesenchyme, so ZFIN records on those parts do not attach.

gene_breadth.note: how many blueprint nodes each gene touches by direct record; a gene in many nodes is pleiotropic, not a fin gene

gene_id_rules.note: Bgee 15.2 and ZFIN's ensembl_1_to_1 table use different Ensembl releases. A Bgee gene whose Ensembl id is absent from ZFIN's table is merged onto the ZFIN gene with exactly the same symbol; otherwise it keeps its Ensembl id as its key. Medaka genes keep Ensembl ids (no ZFIN).

fin_size.why: Fin presence is generic to fish; what is distinctive in flying fish is the size and proportion of the paired fins. Fin size is an organ-level proportion, which connects to Thompson's scaling claims; no scaling is computed here.

verified_leads.finding: Gain-of-function mutations in the potassium channel kcnk5b (the 'another longfin' mutant) give proportionally enlarged fins in zebrafish.
verified_leads.link_type: sufficient for (an increase in fin size, not for making a fin)

verified_leads.finding: The classic longfin (t2) mutant is a regulatory kcnh2a allele that overexpresses this potassium channel and elongates the fins.

verified_leads.finding: A phylogenomic study of flying fishes found signatures of convergent paired-fin enlargement and, intersected with zebrafish fin-size mutants, implicated lat4a and kcnh2a.

verified_leads.symbol_check: lat4a is the symbol used in the paper. ZFIN lists no alias 'lat4a' for slc43a2a (see aliases_check). The identification rests on two independent records: (1) nomenclature: human SLC43A2 is aliased LAT4, 'L-type amino acid transporter 4' (NCBI Gene 124935), and zebrafish slc43a2a is the 'a' paralog of slc43a2 (NCBI Gene 393221; genotype/cache/ncbi_gene_slc43a2.json); (2) ZFIN curated PMID 34534441 itself to slc43a2a: see zfin_rows_citing_this_paper. Settled by the Genotype session on 2026-10-31.

zfin_rows_citing_this_paper.note: ZFIN's curators attached this paper's fin-length phenotypes to slc43a2a (allele dmh26), which is how ZFIN records the paper's lat4a. The homozygous dmh26 rows enter the map as 'required for' links only if they pass the same rules as every other row.

footnotes: * SNP position relative to medaka protein
† SNP in not present in outgroup species
** Present in at least 7/9 sequenced flying fish species (Exocoetidae)
‡ see Supplemental Table X for full list of fin and limb genes
convergent_substitution_in_the_papers_ow.reading: The paper's convergence table lists lat4a under medaka Ensembl id ENSORLG00000009715 with a convergent amino-acid substitution F326L present in the gliding halfbeaks E. viridis and O. micropterus and in at least 7 of 9 sequenced flying-fish species, and flags it in the fin screens. Ensembl names ENSORLG00000009715 SLC43A2 (solute carrier family 43 member 2). So the paper's lat4a is the medaka SLC43A2 gene, which is the human LAT4 ortholog family and ZFIN's slc43a2a: a second confirmation of the identity beside ZFIN's curation of the paper.

source.paper: Daane JM et al. 2021, Modulation of bioelectric cues in the evolution of flying fishes, Curr Biol, doi 10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054, PMID 34534441
source.what_was_measured: paired fin and standard fish lengths of beloniform specimens in the Harvard Museum of Comparative Zoology (paper's STAR Methods); columns: SL (cm), pectoral (cm), pelvic (cm), pectoral/SL, pelvic/SL
caveats: lengths of preserved museum specimens, not live fish; no mass, no fin area, no aspect ratio, no glide data
pectoral/SL recomputed here from the length columns; the sheet's own ratio column is kept beside it
one specimen row (fish 1) has a pelvic/SL cell of ~2.4e-16 in the sheet, an apparent spreadsheet artefact; the recomputed value is used
species names as typed in the sheet

not_sourced: Any flying-fish (Exocoetidae) expression or phenotype record: none exists in Bgee or ZFIN.
Medaka phenotypes: no medaka phenotype database was queried; medaka links are Bgee expression only.
Bgee SPARQL endpoint: refused (HTTP 403, a Cloudflare challenge page); Bgee bulk call files were used instead.
Bgee REST expr_calls page: HTTP 200 with no expression calls for the parameters tried.
Stage for Bgee links: the anatomy-only call files merge stages; Bgee links carry no stage.
ZP term identifiers: ZFIN's EQ annotations (ZFA + PATO) were used; they were not converted to ZP IDs.

fixes: Gene keys: Bgee Ensembl ids absent from ZFIN's 1:1 table are merged onto the ZFIN gene with the identical symbol (summary.gene_id_rules); fgf10a and shha no longer appear twice.

Experimental condition: phenotype rows are kept only under ZFIN 'standard conditions' (ZECO:0000103), matched through phenotype_fish.txt and pheno_environment_fish.txt. The clean file turned out to be almost entirely standard conditions already; what is rejected is mostly annotations that ZFIN also recorded under a treatment experiment and that the join cannot tell apart (ambiguous), plus a few uniquely non-standard rows (summary.zfin_phenotype.rejected, conditions_of_rejected_rows, which lists every condition among the candidate experiments of rejected rows, standard conditions included).

Loss of function: every 'required for' phenotype link carries loss_of_function_evidence; homozygous alleles that also have a heterozygous phenotype and no truncating consequence are rejected as 'loss of function not established' instead of being typed 'required for'.
lat4a = slc43a2a settled on two records (fin_size.verified_leads[2].symbol_check); the aliases check now reads the symbol column.
still_open: ZFIN records attach only where the blueprint has a node with an ontology cross-reference; 16 of 257 cell types have a ZFA equivalent, so the cell layer is capped by the crosswalk.
Bgee links carry no stage (anatomy-only call file). Body-level Bgee links are whole-organism samples, real but not body-plan evidence.
GO system mapping misses musculoskeletal, integumental and other systems (no GO term 'results in development of' their Uberon term).
No ZP identifiers; ZFIN EQ annotations stand in. No medaka phenotype source.

slimming.rule: evidence trimmed; 'expressed in' links capped at 150 per node; derived links dropped (counts kept in nodes)

crosswalk_rule: ZFIN records attach only through Uberon hasDbXref ZFA or ZFA xref CL. Never by name. Medaka data comes only from Bgee, which annotates medaka samples to Uberon itself; no MFO term was mapped by this thread.
